title: mcpsnoop capture envelope
description: One line of an mcpsnoop capture. A capture is JSON Lines with one envelope per line. Fields are only ever added and never change meaning, so a reader ignores the ones it does not know. docs/CAPTURE_FORMAT.md is the prose version of this contract.

session_id.description: The session this envelope belongs to. An opaque name; one file can hold several sessions.

server_label.description: The --label given to mcpsnoop, or a name taken from the server command on stdio and the target's host on HTTP.

seq.description: Position in the session, from 1, rising by one per envelope in the order mcpsnoop read them, so a frame comes before anything sent in answer to it. A jump means envelopes never reached the file.

ts.description: When mcpsnoop read the frame, RFC 3339 with the machine's UTC offset and up to nanosecond precision.

direction.description: c2s is a frame from the client, s2c a frame from the server, stderr a line the server wrote to stderr, meta the session's description. A later release may add a value; skip an envelope whose direction you do not know.

transport.description: The channel the envelope was observed on. A later release may add a value.

raw.description: The frame when it arrived as valid JSON, as a JSON value rather than a string, with insignificant whitespace removed. On a meta envelope it is the session's description.

text.description: A stderr line, a protocol line that was not valid JSON, or the kept part of a frame cut at 16 MiB.

mcp_method.description: The Mcp-Method header of an HTTP request.

mcp_name.description: The Mcp-Name header of an HTTP request.

mcp_protocol_version.description: The MCP-Protocol-Version header of an HTTP request.

mcp_param_headers.description: The Mcp-Param-* headers of an HTTP request, sorted by name.

batch.description: The frame was one element of a JSON-RPC batch on HTTP.

conn_id.description: The client end of the TCP connection an HTTP frame travelled on, as host:port.

exchange.description: Numbers the HTTP request a frame belongs to, from 1. The request's frame and every frame of its response share it.

undelivered.description: On mcpsnoop's own 502, the target refused the connection, so the request never reached it.

truncated.description: This copy of the frame was cut at 16 MiB and is in text. The whole frame still reached the other side.

redacted.description: mcpsnoop's own redaction rewrote this envelope.

status.description: The HTTP status of the response a server frame arrived on.

auth_challenge.description: That response's WWW-Authenticate header, every challenge joined with a comma and a space.

sessionMeta.description: The raw of a meta envelope, which is always the first envelope of a session.

command.description: The server command on stdio, null on HTTP.

cwd.description: The directory the server ran in, on stdio.

target.description: The HTTP endpoint with the userinfo, every query value and the fragment removed. It names the server and is not meant to be dialled.

transportHeaders.description: The HTTP headers the transport specification makes rules about. A request carries what the client sent, a server frame carries the response's content_type, and an empty object is a response with no Content-Type.

traceContext.description: The W3C trace context headers of an HTTP request, as sent. baggage is not recorded.

mcpParamHeader.description: One Mcp-Param-* request header. name is Go's canonical spelling whatever the client sent, so compare it case-insensitively.

redacted.description: mcpsnoop's own redaction replaced the value.
